_comment: Proposed fixes for Hallandale Beach: shown as the infographic timeline on hallandale-beach/index.html.
Hand-curated. Review about once a quarter: update status, cost, and outcome, add new projects.
date      YYYY-MM-DD (or YYYY-MM-01 / YYYY-01-01 when only month or year is known)
summary   one or two plain sentences: what it is
status    Planned | In design | In progress | Completed | Revised | On hold
cost      { usd: number, label: text shown on the page }
outcome   what it does or has done, in plain words
sources   at least one { name, url }. Entries without a source are skipped.
inTotal   optional. false = cost is part of a bigger item, so it is left out of the total

items.title: CDBG drainage improvements, design
items.summary: Design and construction inspection contract for a neighborhood drainage project paid for with federal Community Development Block Grant money.
items.outcome: Design phase only. The construction budget has not been published.

items.title: Vulnerability assessment and adaptation plan
items.summary: State-funded study modeling high tides, sea level rise, and combined rain and tide flooding through 2050 and 2080.
items.outcome: Ranks Hallandale Beach among Broward's most flood-vulnerable areas. Recommends engineered swales, a coordinated seawall plan for Golden Isles, and flood barriers.

items.title: Northeast quadrant injection wells
items.summary: Injection wells that push stormwater deep underground so streets in the city's northeast quadrant drain faster.
items.outcome: Recommended for a 50% state cost share in Florida's 2025-26 Resilient Florida plan.

items.title: NW, SW, and NE stormwater drainage
items.summary: New and upgraded drainage pipes and structures across three quadrants of the city.
items.outcome: Recommended for a 50% state cost share in Florida's 2025-26 Resilient Florida plan.

items.title: NE 14th Avenue pump station
items.summary: A new stormwater pumping station for one of the city's most flood-prone corridors, funded mainly by a federal grant.
items.outcome: Finished in 2022. Heavy rain and a king tide still flooded parts of the city in September 2026, and residents asked for more.
